sweep.every_firing_hand_verified: all 42, by objdump plus the pool arithmetic. temp.elf (28): the AES S-box at 0x1a358, the inverse S-box at 0x1a458 and the Rcon/xtime table at 0x1a558, plus nine further .rodata objects. trap (8): the four string literals main prints, .data at 0x281c via a PREDICATED addge pair, and .bss at 0x2828 twice from atexit/pthread_atfork; also __atexit_handler_wrapper at 0x540, the function pointer atexit passes. 1337ARM.bin, armageddon, entrymain_arm, fmt_arm (1 each): call_gmon_start / call_weak_fn composing _GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_, which lands exactly on each image's .got section address. picpool_arm_le32 (2): the fixture's own two pairs.
sweep.no_edge_on_x86_or_pe: zero firings on every x86-64, i386, ARM64, MIPS, PPC and PE image in the sweep. A RIP-relative load already encodes the address it forms, and SLEIGH folds it into one decode-time constant, so no separate PC constant is ever materialised for the fold to taint.
sweep.additive_by_construction: the change only ever calls st.file with an extra Data edge -- it touches neither queue, neither the discovered function set nor drefs -- so no row can be lost. Confirmed empirically: strings sets identical, 0 owners dropped, and the 15 images kuna already failed or timed out on have identical exit codes on both builds.
sweep.decompiled_c_unchanged: structurally: the xref index is read-only, commits nothing into the engine, and its only consumers are kuna strings / kuna xrefs / kuna decompile-all. make test (675/675) and make test-stages (654/654) confirm.

decisions: The refuter's diagnosis is UPHELD, including its crate correction (kuna-analysis/src/listing, not kuna-decomp) and its refusal to merge this need with arm-literal-pool-disassembly. Its proposed shape -- compose the pool word with the PC of the add and file the edge on the instruction -- is what shipped.

One thing the refuter did not name and it is the reason the option sweep found nothing: this image maps entirely below 0x1000, so ScalarOperandAnalyzer.checkOperands' 4096 floor rejects EVERY address in it. kuna xrefs --from main reported five rows, all calls, and not one data reference of any kind. The composed address therefore cannot be run through that floor -- the floor asks whether an immediate is an address or an integer, and the PC has already settled that. Landing in a mapped section is the whole test.

The PC taint is the guard, not the pool read. `add r0,r0,#4` on the same word lands on a real literal in the fixture, and the only thing separating it from a reference is that the program never read the PC; the fold reports a value only when BOTH a pool word and a constant materialised from the instruction's own address contributed to it.

Values are keyed by the address they reach rather than held as 'the previous instruction's state'. xrefs::build_with_focus walks a function breadth-first, so at a conditional branch the two successors interleave in the queue and 'the instruction decoded before this one' is not the instruction that precedes it.

Only a value that lands in a REGISTER is reported. The GOT idiom `ldr r1,[pool]; ldr r1,[pc,r1]` composes its slot address into a temporary and dereferences it -- filing that would claim a reference the instruction does not form, which is the same rule kuna_picbase already applies to an indexed array base.
Seeding is confined to words kuna_poolref DECLINED, so the two mechanisms never claim one pool word and no target is filed twice.
No option, no phases.toml row, no catalog counter and no tests/stages case: tooling track. The xref index commits nothing into the engine and cannot change emitted C.

The five candidate options whose prose mentions ARM literal pools or references (poolentry, ptrentry, operand_refs, listing, aif) were each re-run against the probe with --option <name> on: all five still report xrefs_count 0 and functions []. No existing option covers this.
speed_method: warmup discarded, 11 repeats, median reported; both arms measured on an otherwise idle machine, the ablation done by shadowing picrefs with an empty Vec

speed_note: the fixed cost is one HashMap::is_empty check per decoded instruction plus a scan of the instruction's ops for a constant-address LOAD; the fold itself runs only where a pool value is in flight.
